rules.body: Apply when edits become deferred persistent work while preserving existing behavior. TASK: "Coalesce edits using the existing trailing-task utility: after a 120 ms quiet\ninterval, write only the latest text in that editing burst. Subsequent bursts\nmust continue to save." TASK: "Preserve the editor's other behavior and public interfaces."

Replace the pending text and restart the quiet interval on each edit; retain the reusable task after consumption. src/services.js: "push(text) { if (ticket !== null) timers.cancel(ticket); value = text; ticket = timers.schedule(flush, wait); }," Verify no write before the latest edit's 120 ms interval expires, one write containing the latest text afterward, and normal saving for a subsequent burst.

Bind deferred work to the document selected when the edit is accepted, rather than looking up the active document when saving. src/coordinator.js: "edit(text){const view=getView();if(view){env.store.write(view.id,text);}}" and "trailing(env.timers,120,text=>env.store.write(id,text))". docs/host-api.md: "All source identities/text and status payloads retain original semantics." Check identity across navigation and preserve valid empty text.

Keep buffer ownership separate from subscription retirement. docs/host-api.md: "Document buffers are owned by the coordinator dictionary, while Badge owns only a live subscription." README.md: "A workspace document buffer persists independently of the current view badge." A departing badge may stop its subscription without cancelling coordinator-owned unsaved work.

When preserving synchronous persistence across departure, flush the departing document's pending work during open, close, and dispose, and consume its scheduled write to prevent duplication. This follows from TASK: "Preserve the editor's other behavior and public interfaces." and docs/host-api.md: "Store read/write/subscribe is synchronous; timer schedule(callback,delay), cancel(handle) is explicitly controlled." Verify persisted text at departure return and no later duplicate write.

Clear the consumed burst before invoking the store callback so synchronous reentry cannot consume it again or erase newly queued work. src/services.js: "const flush = () => { const saved = value; retire(); if (saved !== null) consume(saved); };" Reuse this ordering when flushing at lifecycle boundaries.

Release the departing active view before a callback-capable save, then check whether the initiating navigation still has authority before publishing a destination or clearing rendered state. docs/host-api.md: "A store listener may call navigation synchronously." src/coordinator.js: "const mine=++request;retire();if(true&&mine!==request)return;" Verify that navigation performed by a save listener remains authoritative for both open and close paths.

Do not transfer persistent-document departure policy to transient preview work or to systems with a different documented owner. TASK: "The adjacent search preview is outside this maintenance change." src/services.js: "const task = trailing(timers, 40, query => publish({query}));" and "return {query: text => task.push(text), hide: () => task.cancel()};" Preserve the preview's quiet interval, cancellation, and reuse.

limitations: Departure flushing before return is a preservation inference from existing synchronous persistence and independent document-buffer ownership; TASK does not explicitly require flush().
The public sources do not specify exception recovery or arbitrary reentry from timer scheduling, subscription registration, view access, or rendering callbacks.
AST findings identify review candidates, not proven execution paths or defects; inline-script analysis does not establish Vue runtime behavior.
Evaluation observations and automatic contracts supply no additional business requirements. Passing examples once does not establish causality, exhaustive correctness, or benefit on other tasks.

These rules concern deferred persistence with synchronous callbacks and distinct ownership lifetimes; they do not establish requirements for asynchronous completion or lazy shared-resource consumption.
